answer.evidence: The threshold mapping is in radon/metrics.py:150-157, in mi_rank(score). The docstring says A if score > 19, B if 9 < score <= 19, C if score <= 9. The code is `chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0))`. At score 9 both terms are 1, so the result is 'C'. At 19 only the second term is 1, so it is 'B'. At 19.01 it is 'A'. The code matches the docstring at both thresholds, and both boundaries are inclusive on the lower grade. I found no off-by-one. The review should add boundary tests for 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01. Both handoff_refs/B.txt and C.txt contain only generic text with no file-specific priority. I read the convention as excluding B and C, so the preferred pair is A (raw.py) and D (visitors.py). I gave them 20 minutes each, which is 40 minutes on the pair. I put the other 20 minutes on metrics.py. A grep of raw.py, visitors.py and complexity.py found no mapping of a maintainability score to grades. So the decoded pair is probably only worth checking for callers or inputs to the score, and metrics.py is the primary file. B (complexity.py) gets 0 minutes, since its only match was the unrelated ALPHA lambda.
